Measures need to be put in place to better address corporate rogues. Close taxation loopholes and there must be a substantial increase in enforcement and penalties on corporate misconduct.

analystStatement.en: Rebekha Sharkie: "I supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (Making Multinationals Pay Their Fair Share—Integrity and Transparency) Bill in 2023 as I believe in the principles of fairness. This is a belief that is shared and resonates across Australia. Working Australians see their hard-earned dollars whittled away by taxes while multinational companies that are earning millions, and in some cases billions, pay little or no tax, and they have every right to be frustrated and angry. This bill to make multinationals pay their fair share is just one positive step in a process of urgently required taxation reform. This bill supports a coordinated, global effort to set a 15 per cent global minimum tax and domestic minimum tax for all multinational enterprise groups with an annual revenue of at least $1.2 billion."

label.en: There should be fewer tax breaks on investment properties.

analystStatement.en: Announcing the Coalition's new housing policy at a greenfield housing site outside of Perth on Saturday, Opposition Leader Peter Dutton has maintained the Coalition isn't considering negative gearing either. "Taking supply out of the housing market isn't going to help anyone," said Mr Dutton.

partyStatement.en: The Coalition does not support the abolition of negative gearing or changes to the Capital Gains Tax discount. These changes would cause the supply of rental properties to dry up and further drive up rents (which have skyrocketed by 18 per cent under Labor). Negative gearing is also not a special "tax break" for investment properties, it is a reflection of the principle applied throughout our tax system that tax should be applied to profits (i.e. revenue earned after allowing for legitimate expenses incurred in obtaining it), rather than just to revenue. There are more than 1 million Australians who negatively gear an investment property. They are generally not rich, with around two-thirds of those declaring a net rental loss on a property having a taxable income of $80,000 or less. Seven out of 10 people with rental properties only have 1 property. Teachers, nurses and emergency services personnel are some of the largest negative gearing occupations.

analystStatement.en: The Albanese government was quick to say it was not considering changes to negative gearing ahead of the next election.

partyStatement.en: The Albanese Government is not proposing to change negative gearing or the capital gains tax discount arrangements.

analystStatement.en: Negative gearing and the capital gains discount put billions of dollars in the pockets of property speculators who go to auctions and bid up the price of housing. The Greens have been calling for significant changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax discounts for successive election cycles. At the 2022 election the Greens called for negative gearing to be scrapped beyond a single investment property, and limits put on the capital gains tax discount.

partyStatement.en: Both major parties are handing $176b in tax handouts to wealthy property investors, including negative gearing. The Greens want to phase out tax handouts: Scrap the tax handouts to wealthy property investors with more than one investment property, including negative gearing (it’s stopping renters buying their first home).

analystStatement.en: [One Nation Leader] Pauline Hanson: "[The Greens'] call to get rid of capital gains discounts and negative gearing will suppress property investment and also reduce the availability of rental properties. The Greens do not understand that we must incentivise property investment to increase rental availability and reduce rental prices."

partyStatement.en: It shouldn't be easier to buy an investment property than a home.  But transition needs to be managed carefully.

analystStatement.en: While I do not support alterations to negative gearing, if elected, I will strongly advocate for expert review into affordable housing and rental accommodation, including an increase to rental assistance that ensures it keeps pace with the CPI.

partyStatement.en: All taxes should be reviewed and that may warrant changes to Negative Gearing and CGT, however switching state Stamp Duty for Land Tax would likely most benefit communities.

I want to see a serious process of tax reform to reduce the burden on working people but have not committed to any specific tax changes in advance. The tax change that will increase home ownership most is replacing stamp duty with land tax.

There is a growing intergenerational inequity for access to affordable housing, in part, as a result of generous taxation concessions on investment properties. A gradual scaled reduction of tax benefits on investment properties should be considered.
We need private sector, local, mum and dad investment in housing (not foreign). We need to remove all the onerous restrictions to make housing more affordable.

label.en: How much should wealthier people pay in taxes?

analystStatement.en: The Coalition could ditch its ambition to abolish a tax bracket and extend tax cuts for high earners over fears of fuelling inflation, Peter Dutton has said. The opposition leader told the ABC's RN Breakfast a federal government "spending spree" had worsened inflation and would undermine the case to restore the Coalition's original stage 3 tax cuts, which Labor redesigned in January. "I think it just depends on where the numbers are as we go into the election and how much money is available and how we prioritise our spending," he said. "I think the priority, to be honest, is to get inflation down, to get interest rates down and to support jobs in the economy … I think we're coming into a difficult period. I think a lot of families [are] well and truly experiencing that difficulty."

partyStatement.en: The Coalition does not support wealth taxes. The Coalition does support a progressive tax system on income. Currently, those in the top tax bracket (5 per cent of taxpayers) pay 40 per cent of all income tax collected. All three stages of the personal income tax cuts delivered over recent years, which delivered tax relief to all Australians and protected against bracket creep by making personal taxes simpler and flatter, were fully funded by the previous Coalition government. With personal taxes paid up by 22 per cent under Labor, the Coalition supports providing further income tax relief to hardworking Australians, as soon as we can get the budget position back under control.

analystStatement.en: The government will halve the stage 3 tax cuts for the highest earners and use the money to deliver an $804 tax cut across the board. [...] But Mr Albanese will tell the press club the reversal was motivated by changing economic circumstances, citing Treasury advice that the legislated cuts no longer make sense in a high-inflation environment.

partyStatement.en: The Albanese Government is committed to a progressive and sustainable tax system. Our tax cuts for every taxpayer are focussed on Middle Australia, but deliver cuts all the way up the income scale as aspiration is a fundamental Labor value. Whether you’re earning $50,000, or $90,000 or $190,000 or more – Labor knows you work hard for it.

analystStatement.en: The Greens today have announced a Parliamentary Budget Office-costed plan to tax Australia’s billionaires, as a new revenue measure in the party’s Robin Hood reforms. A core message of the Greens’ plan for minority government is taxing big corporations and billionaires to pay for essential services. [...] Under the plan, Australia’s 150 billionaires would pay an annual 10% tax on their net wealth with a 10% limit on capital flight in any year. The plan is expected to raise $23 billion over the forward estimates and $50 billion over the decade.

partyStatement.en: In a wealthy country like ours, everyone should be able to afford the basics: a home, food, and world-class health and education. Yet billionaires are making out like bandits – while everyone else is being squeezed. They’re making on average $67,000 per hour (over 1,300 times the average hourly wage in Australia). It shouldn’t be controversial: Gina Rinehart should not have $40.6 billion in her pocket while millions in this country are resorting to sleeping in tents and cars. It’s time we turned the tables and made billionaires pay their fair share to fund the services people need. The Greens have a plan to make Australia’s 150 billionaires pay an annual 10% tax on their net wealth. Our plan would raise $50 billion over the decade to fund getting dental into Medicare, making it free to see the GP, and 50 cent public transport fares.

analystStatement.en: [One Nation Leader] Pauline Hanson will reluctantly vote for Labor’s changes to the stage 3 tax cuts, despite saying Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has ‘lied to the Australian people’. Senator Hanson said her party would support the changes, but only because too many people would miss out otherwise. “I have to, because like I said, you don’t crucify all Australians who are struggling and need these tax cuts which is important to the Australian people,” she told Sky News on Wednesday.

partyStatement.en: Australia has a progressive tax system.

analystStatement.en: Families have just been hit with the 11th interest rates rise, and we are yet to feel the impact of the last 10 interest rates rises. This is like death by a thousand cuts. For this reason, I will continue to appeal to the Prime Minister and Treasurer to significantly redesign the stage 3 tax cuts for the super-rich now.

partyStatement.en: Tax reform should be evidence based and systematic, not aimed at specific cohorts in society.
Australia is overly reliant on personal income tax as a proportion of total revenue. More tax should be collected from multinational corporations and fossil fuel companies.
I want to see a serious process of tax reform to reduce the burden on working people but have not committed to any specific tax changes in advance.

analystStatement.en: In what would be a complete overhaul of Australia’s income tax model – Mr Katter said his split income proposal would create greater parity between a couple with double income and no kids (DINKS) and a family of four or five. [...] “So it’s pretty simple, if you’re the sole income earner for a family of five (or however many children), you’re income should be split among your dependants before tax is calculated. That means $100,000 five ways – income $20,000 each – you’re paying virtually no tax.” Mr Katter said he noted providing extensive cuts to families would impact government revenue, which he said should be countered by a 5 per cent primage charge on all goods being imported into the country.

label.en: How much power should trade unions have in the workplace?

analystStatement.en: A Dutton Coalition Government will: [...] Curtail union militancy in Australian workplaces.

partyStatement.en: Australians should have the choice to join a union or not join a union. The Albanese Government have given unions unrestricted power in the workplace, which has led to parts of the construction sector being overrun by criminals and parts of the economy at the mercy of militant unions, such as the NSW train strikes.

analystStatement.en: The CFMEU will be forced to accept an administrator, as the [Labor] government has struck a deal with the Coalition to pass laws to take control of the troubled construction union. [...] The legislation enables a scheme of administration to be set over the construction division of the CFMEU, and allow the Fair Work Commission to appoint an administrator.

partyStatement.en: The Albanese Government has legislated to improve access to collective bargaining for workers and the rights of union delegates.

analystStatement.en: The Australian Greens believe that: [...] Organised labour and strong and enforced workers' rights are fundamental to the achievement of a democratic and equitable economy.

partyStatement.en: Every worker deserves fair pay, secure jobs, and safe conditions. But right now, big corporations are raking in massive profits while millions of workers struggle with stagnant wages, job insecurity, and unsafe workplaces. The major parties have let workplace laws favour corporations over workers, making it harder to get a stable job, negotiate better pay, and stand up for fair treatment. The Greens are working to change that. We believe every worker should have strong rights, secure employment, and wages that keep up with the cost of living. By strengthening workplace protections, supporting unions, and ensuring all jobs are fair and safe, we can build a more equal and prosperous society where no one is left behind.

analystStatement.en: [One Nation Leader] Pauline Hanson: "I've seen the thuggery that's happened in the Parliament, with the Labour Party - the ABCC, that was bought in to help the workers out - not the workers, but the businesses and contractors and people who had to face their unions and their thuggery and bulling. And, uh, it was addressed then the Labor Party came in and undid it. All these people that elected Parliament, the ministerial positions, that's all handpicked by the Labour Party as well - by the unions, I should say, who's dictating to the Prime Minister what factions sit in what seats."

partyStatement.en: Unions have a role to play, but their dominance has contributed to a very complicated industrial relations system.
Depends on the industry and the union.
Depends on the behaviour and nature of the union.
I think the industrial relations changes in this term of parliament have gone too far and this needs to be redressed.
There is a careful balance needed between protecting workers rights and ensuring that effective operations of business.
Unions play a very important and essential role in supporting employees. But this role should not be open to abuse.

label.en: How much should out-of-work Australians receive in unemployment benefits?

analystStatement.en: The federal government has committed in the federal budget to lifting the base rate of JobSeeker by $40 per fortnight and extending eligibility for a higher rate to people over 55. [...] As an alternative, Mr Dutton said the government should consider making it easier for JobSeeker recipients to work more. "We think the better approach is to allow people on the JobSeeker payment to work say five or 10 hours a fortnight," Mr Dutton said. "It would give them a lot of extra money in their pocket compared to the $40 that the government is offering."

partyStatement.en: The Coalition's key focus is on creating jobs and getting people back into work because we know that getting a job is the best way to improve the living standards of people and their families. The JobSeeker Payment is not a salary or wage replacement. It is a safety net for people while they look for work. Few countries provide the strong safety net that is available to Australians. Because the JobSeeker Payment is funded by taxpayers it needs to be managed responsibly. This responsibility extends to future generations who will have to meet the cost of the social security system in the decades to come.

analystStatement.en: Despite pressure from advocacy bodies to raise the JobSeeker rate to at least $80 a day, the rate will remain at $55.79 for singles with no dependants, and $59.75 for singles with a dependent child and Australians over 55.

partyStatement.en: Labor has made significant investments to strengthen the safety net, providing an additional $11.5 billion for social security payments. This includes delivering a $40 per fortnight increase to working-age and student payments, including JobSeeker. In recognition that some people can face additional barriers to finding employment and need more support, we also expanded eligibility for the higher rate of Jobseeker to Australians aged 55 and over who are on payment for nine months or more, and to those with an assessed partial capacity to work of 0-14 hours per week. Since Labor was elected, the base rate of JobSeeker for single recipients with no dependent children has increased by $138 a fortnight or 22 per cent. This is an extra $3,600 in additional support in people’s pockets each year.  We’ve delivered the first back-to-back increases to Commonwealth Rent Assistance in over 30 years, to help people on income support, pensioners and low-income families to manage rental pressures. Combined with indexation, this means maximum rates of rent assistance have increased by 45 per cent since Labor was elected. In addition, for single parents who face the difficult challenge of balancing work and care on their own, the Government has expanded eligibility for Parenting Payment Single until their youngest child turns 14, up from 8.

analystStatement.en: The Greens have a plan to end poverty in Australia and ensure support is there for everyone who needs it, no matter what. This starts with raising the rate of all Centrelink income support payments above the poverty line.

partyStatement.en: The Greens are the only party that has consistently voted to lift income support payments above the poverty line, and pushed for reducing the age pension age to 65.

analystStatement.en: [One Nation Leader Pauline] Hanson wants welfare stripped right back to encourage Aussies to take up jobs. Her policy is that the dole should only be available for two years out of every five for recipients capable of working. 'I'd like to see a lot of them get off their backsides and go and start working,' Senator Hanson said. 'Instead we're have fourth generations sitting on the bloody dole in this country and they think it's a way of life for them.'

partyStatement.en: Trapping people in poverty is not good for the economy or consistent with our egalitarian and compassionate values.
I support an increase in Jobseeker to the level of the aged pension.
The rate of unemployment benefits should align with the aged pension.
60% of households relying on JobSeeker live below the poverty line.

According to the Australia Council of Social Services, JobSeeker is currently just $56 a day and Youth Allowance just $47 a day. Both rates are less than half the minimum wage and leave people unable to afford basic necessities such as rent, food and medicine and limit ability to return to paid employment.
We must ensure there are sufficient incentives in place to encourage work and contributions. The fulfilment that comes from working.
Every effort should be made to meaningfully assist working age Australians into training and employment. Flexible and tailored investment is needed to ensure every Australian can be aspirational.

label.en: The government should change its tax policies to discourage people from using housing as an investment.
People who own more than one property should not receive property tax breaks.
